newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Manufacturing shares dip on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturing shares dip on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Shares in some of Nigeria's biggest manufacturing companies fell on Tuesday while sustained demand for oil marketing companies and breweries kept the index buoyant.
The all-share index closed at 6,879.72 from 6,860.45 on Monday.
Lever Brothers fell 30 kobo to 21.60 naira, Cadbury was down 10 kobo to 23.80 naira and Ashaka Cement slid to 17.70 naira, 20 kobo lower.
Packaging firm Carnaud Metal Box dropped by the maximum five percent allowed to 2.85 naira from 3.00 naira. Tyre maker Dunlop was down 10 kobo at 9.90.
Afribank was 10 kobo down at 4.50 naira. Union Bank had one kobo shaved off its Monday close to end at 5.39 naira.
Traders said undiminished sales of the stocks depressed their prices as investors either tried to take profits or move investments to other sectors.
Demand for oil marketing company Agip saw its shares rise 45 kobo to 21.05 naira.
"Agip posted one of the best mid year results in the oil sector and investors wanted to raise their holding because of its relatively cheap price," an analyst said.
Unipetrol rose 40 kobo to 53.60 naira, African Petroleum, Mobil and Total added 30 kobo apiece to 42.60 naira, 47.00 naira and 55.30 naira respectively.
Nigerian Breweries finished 40 kobo higher at 18.00 naira. Guinness rose by 25 kobo to 7.35 naira.
AIICO Insurance closed 40 kobo higher at 11.10 naira.
